ai.description: This file implements the LedgerMaster class, which is a core component of the XRPL server responsible for managing the lifecycle, state, and history of ledgers. It handles tracking the current, validated, and published ledgers, manages ledger acquisition and validation, and coordinates the publication and storage of ledgers. The class ensures ledger continuity, handles missing or out-of-sync ledgers, and manages fetch packs for ledger synchronization between peers. It also processes held transactions, manages pathfinding requests, and interacts with other subsystems such as the order book database, fee tracking, and amendment management. The file includes logic for advancing the ledger state, handling consensus results, and maintaining caches and history for efficient ledger retrieval. It is central to the operation of the XRPL node, ensuring ledger integrity, synchronization, and network participation.

This file implements the logic for the CreateCheck transaction in the XRPL (XRP Ledger) codebase. It defines three main functions: preflight, preclaim, and doApply. The preflight function performs initial validation checks on the transaction, such as feature enablement, flag correctness, self-check prevention, amount and currency validation, and expiration checks. The preclaim function checks ledger state conditions, ensuring the destination account exists, permissions are correct, trustlines are not frozen, and the check has not already expired. The doApply function creates the Check ledger object, ensures the source account has sufficient reserve, inserts the Check into the appropriate directories for both the source and destination accounts, and updates the owner's count. The code includes detailed error handling and logging for malformed transactions and ledger state issues.

This file implements the core logic for the transaction queue (TxQ) in the XRPL server. The TxQ manages transactions that cannot be immediately applied to the open ledger, handling queuing, prioritization, and eventual application or removal. Key features include: calculation of fee levels paid and required, dynamic adjustment of queue and fee escalation parameters based on ledger activity, logic for replacing or removing transactions in the queue, and mechanisms for applying queued transactions when conditions allow. The queue enforces per-account and global limits, supports transaction replacement with higher fees, and penalizes accounts for repeated failures. The file also provides metrics and RPC reporting for queue status and fee levels. Configuration is supported via a setup function that reads parameters from the server config. The main classes are TxQ (the queue itself), TxQ::FeeMetrics (for fee escalation and queue sizing), TxQ::MaybeTx (a queued transaction), and TxQ::TxQAccount (per-account transaction management).

This file implements various low-level database operations for the XRPL (Ripple) ledger and transaction relational database backend. It provides functions to manage, query, and maintain ledger and transaction data in SQLite databases. Key functionalities include: mapping table types to strings, creating and configuring ledger and transaction databases, retrieving minimum and maximum ledger sequences, deleting ledger data by sequence, counting rows, saving validated ledgers (with integrity checks and serialization), retrieving ledger info by index or hash, fetching transaction history, and paginated account transaction queries. The file also includes logic for checking available database and disk space, and for handling transaction deserialization errors. The code is tightly integrated with the application's logging, configuration, and ledger management subsystems, and makes extensive use of the SOCI C++ database library for SQL operations.

This file defines the LedgerMaster class, which is a central component in managing ledgers within the XRPL (XRP Ledger) server. LedgerMaster is responsible for tracking, accessing, and maintaining the state of various ledgers, including the current, closed, validated, and published ledgers. It provides interfaces for fetching ledgers by sequence or hash, managing ledger history, handling held transactions, and coordinating ledger replay and fetch packs. The class also manages synchronization, validation, and publication of ledgers, as well as metrics collection for ledger ages. It uses various helper classes and data structures for caching, threading, and concurrency control. The file also defines a nested Stats struct for collecting and reporting metrics. Overall, LedgerMaster acts as the authoritative manager for ledger state and transitions in the XRPL server.

This file implements the logic for cashing checks in the XRPL (XRP Ledger) transaction processing system. The main class, CashCheck, provides three key methods: preflight, preclaim, and doApply. The preflight method performs initial validation on the transaction, ensuring the correct feature is enabled, flags are valid, and that either Amount or DeliverMin is specified (but not both). It also checks for valid amounts and currencies. The preclaim method checks the existence and validity of the check in the ledger, verifies permissions, ensures the check has not expired, and validates that the funds, trust lines, and issuer authorizations are sufficient and correct. The doApply method executes the actual cashing of the check, handling both XRP and IOU (issued currency) cases, including trust line creation if needed, fund transfers, and removal of the check from the ledger. It also manages owner counts and applies the changes to the ledger. The code includes detailed error handling and logging for various failure scenarios, ensuring robust transaction processing.

This file implements the doNoRippleCheck RPC handler for the XRPL (Ripple) server. The handler checks an account's 'no ripple' settings and trust lines to ensure they are configured appropriately for the account's role (either 'gateway' or 'user'). It validates input parameters, retrieves the account and its trust lines from the ledger, and identifies potential misconfigurations, such as a gateway not setting the default ripple flag or a user setting it unnecessarily. For each issue found, it adds a description to a 'problems' array in the response. If requested, it also generates suggested transactions to fix the issues, such as AccountSet or TrustSet transactions, and includes them in the response. The helper function fillTransaction constructs these transaction templates with the correct fields and fees. The code ensures proper error handling and input validation throughout.

The class handles database setup, access, and operations such as retrieving ledger and transaction information, deleting old data, saving validated ledgers, paginating account transactions, and checking database space usage. It uses helper functions from the detail namespace for most database operations and manages two main database connections: one for ledgers and one for transactions. The implementation supports optional use of transaction tables, and provides methods for closing databases, getting storage usage, and creating the database instance. The file is a key part of the backend relational database layer for XRPL, enabling efficient storage and retrieval of blockchain data.

This file implements the core transaction processing logic for the XRPL (XRP Ledger) server, specifically the Transactor class and related transaction preflight and application routines. The Transactor class encapsulates the steps required to validate, apply, and manage the effects of a transaction on the ledger. Key responsibilities include: multi-stage preflight validation (checking flags, network ID, account, fee, signatures, etc.), fee calculation and deduction, sequence/ticket management, permission checks (including delegation), and signature verification (single and multi-sign). The class also handles transaction application, including updating account state, consuming sequence numbers or tickets, and managing transaction metadata. Special logic is included for handling batch transactions, dry runs, and error/failure scenarios (such as resetting state and removing expired or unfunded offers, trust lines, and credentials). The operator() method orchestrates the full transaction lifecycle, including invariant checks and error handling. The file also defines several helper functions for cleaning up ledger objects after failed or expired transactions. Overall, this file is central to ensuring that transactions are processed securely, correctly, and efficiently on the XRPL.

ai.description: This file implements the PeerImp class, which represents a peer connection in the XRPL (Ripple) overlay network. PeerImp manages the lifecycle and communication of a peer, including connection setup, message sending and receiving, protocol negotiation, resource usage tracking, and feature support. It handles various protocol messages (transactions, validations, proposals, ledger data, etc.), manages transaction and ledger queues, enforces resource limits, and supports features like transaction reduce-relay, ledger replay, and squelching. The class also tracks peer metrics (latency, bytes sent/received), manages peer status and tracking (converged/diverged), and interacts with other network components such as the job queue, ledger master, validators, and resource manager. The file includes logic for relaying messages, handling protocol errors, charging peers for resource usage, and maintaining peer state for network health and synchronization.

This file implements the core logic for the RCLConsensus class, which manages the consensus process in the Ripple (XRPL) ledger system. It defines the RCLConsensus and its nested Adaptor class, which acts as an interface between the consensus engine and the rest of the application. The Adaptor handles acquiring ledgers and transaction sets, sharing proposals and transactions with peers, proposing new ledgers, managing open transactions, and tracking consensus state. It also manages the process of closing and accepting ledgers, including building new ledgers, applying transactions, handling disputes, and validating ledgers. The file includes mechanisms for voting on fees and amendments, handling negative UNL (Unique Node List) votes, and detecting potential censorship of transactions. It provides detailed logging and status notifications to peers, and manages validator keys and operating modes. The RclConsensusLogger class is used for detailed timing and logging of consensus events. Overall, this file is central to the operation of distributed consensus in the XRPL node software, coordinating ledger agreement, transaction application, and network communication during consensus rounds.

# Ledger Process #

## Introduction ##

## Life Cycle ##

Every server always has an open ledger. All received new transactions are applied to the open ledger. The open ledger can't close until we reach a consensus on the previous ledger, and either: there is at least one transaction in the open ledger, or the ledger's close time has been reached.

When the open ledger is closed the transactions in the open ledger become the initial proposal. Validators will send the proposal (non-validators will simply not send the proposal). The open ledger contains the set of transactions the server thinks should go into the next ledger.
